summary: iter123 — Mappings Wizard (Motive vehicles + future MaintainX assets). All 7 wizard pytests pass + all 23 iter122 integration-center regression pytests pass (30/30). Out-of-band manual checks confirmed: negative-auth on /preview, /commit, /runs all return 401; X-Actor-Name header is reflected in commit response and audit run list; force-overwrite refuse/allow flow works; equipment_master never modified by any wizard call. Frontend Wizard tab loads via [data-testid=ic-tab-wizard], paste CSV → Preview matches button hits /preview → preview panel [data-testid=ic-wizard-preview-panel] renders with category counts and per-row action dropdowns. End-to-end safety guarantees from the PRD all hold.
critical_code_review_comments: wizard.py is ~460 lines — still under the 700-line ceiling but the preview() function is ~120 lines; consider extracting the per-row classifier into a helper for unit testing.

Preview pre-loads up to 20k equipment_master rows + 20k asset_mappings into memory per request. Fine at 342 rows today; if the fleet ever exceeds ~5k rows this becomes the slow path — switch to indexed lookups by unit_number.

_provider_id_field returns dotted string ('motive.vehicle_id') which is then split and walked manually in two places. A small helper `get_external_id_from_mapping(mapping, provider)` would DRY this up.
Audit-log GET /runs has no pagination beyond limit (max 200). For long-term audit history a cursor or skip/limit would be cleaner.
